title: Act V, Scene II

teacherSummary.text: Hamlet tells Horatio how he rewrote Claudius's letter so that Rosencrantz and Guildenstern were executed. Osric brings Laertes's challenge. In the duel Gertrude drinks the poisoned cup; Laertes wounds Hamlet; they exchange swords and Hamlet wounds Laertes. Gertrude dies; Laertes confesses; Hamlet kills Claudius. Laertes and Hamlet forgive each other; Hamlet dies; Fortinbras claims the throne.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “There’s a divinity that shapes our ends, / Rough-hew them how we will” slowly and put it in my own words: Hamlet tells Horatio that a divinity shapes our ends, however roughly we plan them. Next, craft. I notice the image of a craftsman's rough cut finished by a higher hand. The strongest word is “divinity”: it names a guiding power, Providence, beyond human plans. Then, effect. What has Hamlet come to believe before the duel? My answer: Hamlet now trusts fate rather than his own schemes; his calm acceptance prepares him for the duel and his death.
